misclassified_entities.name: Node Operator
misclassified_entities.explanation: The node operator is the entity controlling the node's identity keypair. This is a design-time/operational actor who configures the node, not a runtime data source that sends data into the system during execution.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.description: Peer node sending blocks for validation
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Peer nodes in the P2P network can be malicious actors sending invalid or malformed blocks. All received blocks must be fully validated before acceptance. Invalid blocks trigger InvalidBlock exception and are rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.description: External entity submitting transactions (user or application)
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Transaction submitters can provide invalid transactions with bad signatures, insufficient balance, wrong nonces, or other validation failures. All validation exceptions (InvalidTransaction, InvalidSenderError, InvalidSignatureError) must be handled appropriately.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.description: Remote Ethereum node providing ENR records via P2P protocol
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Peer nodes can provide forged or malformed ENR records. Cryptographic signature verification is required to establish identity binding. Size limits (300 bytes) and format validation prevent resource exhaustion attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Resolver
trusted_external_entities.description: DNS service providing ENR records via DNS discovery
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DNS responses can be spoofed without DNSSEC. However, the cryptographic signature on ENR records limits attack impact to DoS (directing to non-existent nodes) rather than impersonation.

trusted_external_entities.name: ENS Registry
trusted_external_entities.description: Ethereum Name Service providing ENR records
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: ENS data is anchored on-chain and benefits from blockchain immutability. However, ENS entries can be maliciously registered or updated by domain owners. ENR signatures still provide identity verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: DNS Discovery Source
trusted_external_entities.description: External DNS infrastructure providing ENR records - potentially subject to DNS spoofing
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DNS infrastructure can be compromised or spoofed. ENR records from DNS are treated as untrusted until cryptographic validation completes.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Source
trusted_external_entities.description: Remote peer on devp2p network - may be malicious
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any P2P peer can be malicious and attempt to provide fake ENR records. Signature verification is the only trust anchor for node identity.

trusted_external_entities.name: ENS Source
trusted_external_entities.description: Ethereum Name Service resolver - depends on on-chain data integrity
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: ENS resolution depends on blockchain state which has strong integrity guarantees. However, the domain owner controls the ENR content, so signature verification remains necessary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.description: External entity submitting transaction with calldata payload
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Transaction submitters provide calldata that must be charged according to the gas pricing schedule. The new 15/60 gas per byte pricing is designed to prevent DoS through excessive calldata while maintaining economic viability.
